page: Microsoft Azure L2s_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Lsv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU is equipped with 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, and includes 480 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core performance is notable, with a strong Geekbench single-core score of 2138.0 and a strong single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.24 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are limited. The stress-ng multi-core performance is rated poor at 1992.19, and Geekbench multi-core performance is weak at 2622.0. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds falling into the poor category at 20.23 GB/sec and 14.38 GB/sec respectively.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the bundled 480 GB local storage, this instance is structured for workloads requiring moderate memory density and local storage capacity rather than intensive parallel processing. It is suitable for single-threaded tasks, basic database operations, and lightweight text processing. However, it presents a performance tradeoff for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, and large-scale memory-bound operations due to its low multi-core efficiency and restricted memory bandwidth. Qualitatively, it offers an entry-level entry point into the storage-capable Lsv4 family, balancing dedicated high-clock CPU cores with local storage capacity.
